title: " Fresh and Saltwater Fish"
---

# Freshwater Species:

## Trout fishing in New Zealand has a massive following from both local and international anglers. I was humbled by the amazing ecosystems and the giant fish.

![No Market Sells Local Trout](/images/IMG_1335.jpeg)

### Rainbow Trout:

### The typically easier to land species. This one was caught along the Tutaekuri river and was prepared by my Wwoofing (farmstay) hosts.

#### I was able to catch a rainbow trout on my own for the first time early in my trip in a small river near Hamilton

![Biggest Fish on a Dry Fly - Photo by Alex](/images/IMG_2186.PNG)

### Brown Trout:

### These fish led me to some of the most amazing places in the world and created some of the most amazing stories.

#### Hunting for back country brown trout is a highly technical venture

![Uncertain on ID](/images/IMG_2635.jpg)

### Canterbury Mudfish:

### Possibly the highly threatened endemic fish that suffers from trout encrouchment and water quality changes.

![Cultural Icon](/images/eel.jpg)

### Tuna (freshwater eel)

### These eels have persisted and represent resilience throughout the freshwater ecosystems.

#### They have an amazing sense of smell and tried to take our trout

# Saltwater Fish Species:

![Only Catch of the Day](/images/Ed.jpg)

### Snapper:

### Caught on light tackle while viewing a giant swarm of krill on the fish finder

#### Ed was extremely generous to take me out on his boat as he returned it from Auckland

![Very Good Eating](/images/IMG_2520.jpg)

### Kahawai (Australian salmon):

### These fish were caught and smoked. Andrew lent me his gear and I caught them on the tidal flats near the mouth of a culvert

![Splashed out of Water](/images/or.jpg)

### Olive Rockfish:

### Hannah and I decided to try and splash some fish out of the tidal canal while going for a walk.

![First Catch on Squid](/images/IMG_2508.jpg)

### Spotty (notolabrus celidotus):

### An unexpected sight while trying to catch some kahawai.
